summary: Radar for 2026-10-20 (GLP-1 focus). I checked the top signals with live searches. Three stories broke in the last 24–48 h and fit our playbook lanes: (1) Novo's new CagriSema analysis in women: 25% average weight loss vs 3% on placebo at 68 weeks in about 2,300 women from REDEFINE 1, split by menopause stage (CNBC, Oct 20). It's a named new result inside the 48 h window, so it's our best Lane C first-explainer, the closest thing to EloraTZP. (2) A nationwide recall of compounded tirzepatide from Apothecary Pharma: 22 vials, lack of sterility assurance, FDA Class II on Oct 8. Mainstream outlets are running confusing headlines that name Mounjaro and Zepbound, so people are searching 'is my Mounjaro recalled'. That makes a calm Lane B 'what's confirmed' piece urgent. (3) Reuters (Oct 20) on GLP-1 users turning to TikTok-sold supplements, with FDA warning letters on 'GLP-1' drops and patches. This keeps our rising supplements topic going and suits a Lane A search title. Retatrutide gray-market coverage keeps building: the Penn Reddit study is now in Penn Today, SciTechDaily and MedPage; Lilly filed 6 lawsuits in August and 5 more on Oct 8; NL Times reports a rise in the Netherlands and Bloomberg covers Brazil's black market. That supports the second Lane B long-form. The Medscape plateau piece and the OCTANE pill-switch data refresh two evergreen Lane A searches ('weight loss plateau on tirzepatide', 'Wegovy pill vs shot'). I rejected the NY Post '$100 GLP-1 in 48 hours' telehealth promo and law-firm NAION lawsuit content. Reminder for production: 'Is X approved yet?' titles are banned, and no long-form may repeat a Short topic from the last 14 days (sleep apnea, SURMOUNT-5, stomach side effects).

candidates.topic: CagriSema in women: Novo's new REDEFINE 1 analysis shows 25% average weight loss vs 3% on placebo at 68 weeks in about 2,300 women with obesity or overweight, plus results by menopause stage (26.7% premenopausal, 24.8% perimenopausal, 23.1% postmenopausal)
candidates.angle: Lane C first explainer within 48 h: 'CagriSema in Women: What the New Menopause Analysis Shows'. Name the drug first. Explain what cagrilintide (amylin) adds to semaglutide. Label it clearly as an analysis done after the trial, by menopause stage: subgroup averages, not predictions. Note that CagriSema is not FDA-approved as of Oct 2026 (Novo expects a launch early next year, per CNBC) and give its common GI side effects. Do not frame it as 'beat Wegovy': there is no head-to-head in this analysis.
candidates.why_now: Novo released the analysis on Oct 20 and CNBC, Reuters syndication and STAT picked it up the same day. Women and menopause are a large, high-CPM search audience and YouTube has almost no explainers yet. It's a named new result inside the 48 h window, matching the EloraTZP pattern (442 views).

evidence.signal: 25% vs 3% placebo at 68 wks in ~2,300 women; menopause-stage split; launch expected early next year
Wire pickup: 'CagriSema helped women lose 25% of weight on average'
Trade press coverage the same day
CagriSema vs semaglutide 2.4 mg systematic review gives the wider context

candidates.topic: Compounded tirzepatide recall: Apothecary Pharma recalled 22 vials (18 mg/mL multi-dose, lots AP-202622 to AP-202644) for lack of sterility assurance; FDA classed it Class II on Oct 8. Headlines wrongly suggest Mounjaro and Zepbound are affected
candidates.angle: Lane B: 'Tirzepatide Recall: Is Mounjaro or Zepbound Affected?' Answer within 10 seconds: it's a compounded product, credited to the FDA recall notice with its date. Explain what Class II means in the FDA's own words, why compounded vials aren't the FDA-approved pens, and what to do: ask your pharmacist or prescriber about approved options. Calm tone, no scare framing, no emoji, no brand hashtags. Before scripting, confirm on the FDA enforcement report that branded products aren't included.
candidates.why_now: USA Today, NY Post, MassLive, Tennessean, Daily Voice and Yahoo all ran recall stories on Oct 20, several with misleading 'Mounjaro, Zepbound' headlines. That creates big confused search demand that a calm 'what's confirmed' video can answer. Our gray-market and authenticity lane is the strongest we have (median 108).

evidence.signal: 22 vials, lack of sterility assurance, Class II on Oct 8, earlier FDA warning letter Dec 2025
'Compounded GLP-1 injections recalled nationwide: 4 notes'
FDA policy page on compounders now that GLP-1 supply has stabilised

candidates.topic: Retatrutide online: what the FDA and Lilly have confirmed (Oct 2026). Lilly filed 6 lawsuits in August and 5 more on Oct 8 against sellers using 'research use only' labels; the Penn AI Reddit study reached mainstream press Oct 19–20; illegal retatrutide is rising in the Netherlands
candidates.angle: Lane B: 'Retatrutide Online: What the FDA and Lilly Have Confirmed (Oct 2026)'. Use dated, attributed lines only: Lilly's CMO said black-market product 'is not a medicine'; retatrutide is not approved anywhere; Lilly plans to file Q1 2027; the Penn preprint found self-reported symptoms that differ from the trials. Never name sellers. End by pointing to a prescriber about approved options or trials.
candidates.why_now: New coverage is coming from several independent sources: Penn Today, SciTechDaily and MedPage (Oct 19–20), Stocktwits on the lawsuits (Oct 20), NL Times (Oct 19) and Bloomberg on Brazil (Oct 20). Search queries like 'fda concerns unapproved glp-1 retatrutide' keep showing up in the feeds. Our strongest Short lane.

The original 6 lawsuits; Hyman: 'not a medicine'

candidates.topic: Do 'GLP-1 supplements' work? Reuters (Oct 20): GLP-1 users are buying TikTok-sold supplements (berberine, fibre, probiotics, 'GLP-1' drops and patches) while the FDA issues warning letters and weighs tighter rules
candidates.angle: Lane A: 'Do GLP-1 Supplements Work? What the FDA and Studies Say'. Explain what the GLP-1 hormone is, why a supplement isn't the drug or a receptor activator, and what the evidence shows for berberine (small effect) and for fibre and protein (modest effects on your own GLP-1, recommended habits, not a replacement). Include the line 'don't switch, stop or change your current medicines on your own.'
candidates.why_now: The Reuters wire on Oct 20 (syndicated by The Standard HK and Deccan Herald), product launches (NOW 'GLP-1 Metabolic Support') and Nutrition Insight coverage, all on top of a topic already rising in 2 previous snapshots. The search phrase has strong evergreen demand.

evidence.signal: 'As weight-loss drug users turn to dietary supplements, doctors and regulators raise flags'
Doctors raise concerns over supplement use among GLP-1 users

candidates.topic: Weight-loss plateau on semaglutide or tirzepatide: why it happens, plus Medscape's 'Could retatrutide break a GLP-1 plateau?' (Oct 20) and TRIUMPH-1, where no plateau was seen by 80 weeks
candidates.angle: Lane A: 'Weight Loss Plateau on Tirzepatide: Why It Happens'. Cover metabolic adaptation, why trial curves flatten (SURMOUNT-1, STEP 1), and habits linked to keeping results (protein, strength training). Mention retatrutide only as unapproved research with its dated status. No switching or dose advice: 'bring it to your prescriber'.
keywords: why did my weight loss stop on mounjaro
candidates.why_now: The Medscape piece is from today. Plateau searches are some of the most-typed GLP-1 questions, and few science-first explainers exist. Fits the 'Life on GLP-1' series.

evidence.signal: 'Could Retatrutide Break a GLP-1 Weight-Loss Plateau?'
TRIUMPH-1: no plateau seen; 28.3% at 80 wks on the top dose

candidates.topic: Wegovy pill vs Wegovy shot: what's the difference? OCTANE real-world data (EASD, Sept 30): 194 adults who moved from injectable semaglutide or tirzepatide to the oral semaglutide pill lost an average of 4.1% more over 3 months; Men's Journal and Yahoo coverage Oct 20
candidates.angle: Lane A search-question explainer: 'Wegovy Pill vs Wegovy Shot: What's the Difference?' Cover how each is taken (pill water and food rules), trial results in their own populations, and OCTANE's limits (retrospective, telehealth, self-reported, no comparison group, so it doesn't show switching works better). Required line: don't switch on your own; discuss it with your prescriber.
keywords: switching from injection to wegovy pill
candidates.why_now: Consumer coverage on Oct 20 (Men's Journal, Yahoo Creators doctor explainer), Amazon Pharmacy now offers the pill, and there's steady 'pill or shot' search demand. Our earlier pill-vs-shot long-form was a trial deep dive; this is a search-question format with a fresh fact.

evidence.signal: OCTANE: 4.1% in 3 months after switching; 40.7% reached ≥5%
Limitations: retrospective, 194 patients, self-report

The SEMALEAN cohort is observational, so use 'linked to'.
